framed_question: How can the FullCalendar skill be improved? What's missing, weak, redundant, or could be better structured? Consider: clarity, completeness, triggering accuracy, examples, edge cases, anti-patterns, organization, and real-world effectiveness.

advisors.name: The Contrarian
advisors.response: This skill has a fatal structural problem: it's a table of contents pretending to be a skill. The SKILL.md is 6.6KB of pointers to reference files that are themselves 7KB each. An agent reading this gets almost zero actionable information from the entry point — it must read 40KB+ of reference files to answer even basic questions. The 'Critical Rules' section is the only genuinely useful part of SKILL.md, and it's buried after conceptual fluff. The 'Quick Start' is four vague steps that say 'identify what you need' and 'open the matching reference file' — that's not guidance, that's a directory listing. The HTMX integration section is disproportionately large for what is an edge case; most FullCalendar users aren't using HTMX. Meanwhile, there's zero mention of timezone handling, which is the single most common source of production bugs with calendar apps. No mention of recurring events, which FullCalendar handles poorly and every developer gets wrong. The 'Task Routing' table is the right idea but too coarse — 'Handle clicks, selections, drag-drop' maps to callbacks.md, but that file is 7KB and covers 15+ callbacks. The skill needs to answer questions, not point at more files. Every reference file should have a 'Common Mistakes' section, and SKILL.md itself should contain the top 10 pitfalls inline, not make agents hunt for them.

advisors.name: The First Principles Thinker
advisors.response: What problem does this skill actually solve? It exists so that an AI agent can help a developer build or debug a FullCalendar integration. That means the skill must bridge two gaps: (1) the agent doesn't know FullCalendar's API, and (2) the agent doesn't know the common integration patterns for the user's stack. Currently the skill addresses gap #1 with a mini-reference manual split across seven files. But reference manuals already exist — FullCalendar's official docs are excellent. The skill's unique value should be gap #2: the hard-won integration patterns that aren't in the official docs. Things like: how to wire FullCalendar's JSON feed to a Django view that returns paginated events; how to handle CSRF tokens in event CRUD operations; how to make FullCalendar work inside an HTMX partial swap without double-rendering; how to handle timezone conversion between server UTC and calendar display. The current skill mentions these in passing but doesn't solve them. The reference files should be reorganized around integration scenarios, not API surfaces. Instead of 'callbacks.md' listing every callback, have 'event-crud.md' that shows the full round-trip: click → HTMX request → server response → calendar update. The skill should teach the agent to be dangerous with FullCalendar, not just literate.

advisors.name: The Expansionist
advisors.response: This skill is leaving enormous value on the table by staying API-focused. FullCalendar is almost never used in isolation — it's embedded in larger applications with specific needs the skill ignores entirely. Consider: (1) Accessibility. FullCalendar has a11y pitfalls everywhere — keyboard navigation, screen reader announcements for date changes, focus management after drag-drop. Zero mention. (2) Mobile. FullCalendar's timeGrid view is nearly unusable on phones. The skill should guide agents toward responsive view selection and touch-friendly alternatives. (3) Performance. Calendar with 1000+ events? The skill should document virtual rendering, event source refetching strategies, and the `lazyFetching` option. (4) Testing. How do you test a FullCalendar integration? The skill should include Playwright patterns for interacting with calendar views, asserting event rendering, and simulating drag-drop. (5) Framework connectors. The skill says 'use vanilla JS unless the project explicitly uses React/Vue/Angular' — but it doesn't help the agent detect which is in use, or how to adapt patterns. (6) The evals file is a single JSON with no actual test scenarios. This skill should have evals that test whether an agent can actually build a working calendar, not just recite API docs. The skill could be the definitive FullCalendar integration guide, not just a reference mirror.

advisors.name: The Outsider
advisors.response: Reading this skill as someone who's never used FullCalendar and needs to help a developer with it: I'm lost within 30 seconds. The SKILL.md opens with 'Comprehensive reference for FullCalendar v6' but never explains what FullCalendar IS in terms a non-calendar person can grasp. The 'Core Concepts' section introduces five concepts but doesn't explain why any of them matter or how they relate. What's a 'render hook' and when would I need one? The skill assumes I know the difference between dayGrid and timeGrid views — I don't. The reference map is just filenames with one-line descriptions; I can't tell which file I need without opening it. The 'Task Routing' table is the most useful part, but it's at the bottom — put it at the top. Also, the skill has zero code examples in SKILL.md itself. Every other skill I've seen has at least a minimal code snippet showing what success looks like. Here, I'd have to read initialization.md just to see what `new Calendar(el, options)` looks like in context. The 'Critical Rules' section is genuinely excellent — the kind of thing that prevents real bugs. But it has only 8 rules; there are probably 20 more that experienced FullCalendar developers know and beginners learn the hard way. The skill reads like it was written by someone who knows FullCalendar very well and forgot what it's like to not know it.

advisors.name: The Executor
advisors.response: The fastest improvement: restructure SKILL.md to lead with the decision tree, not the encyclopedia. Right now an agent reading this skill has to understand the full reference architecture before it can help. Instead, SKILL.md should be a 200-line decision tree: 'Is this a new calendar? → initialization.md. Is this a bug with events not showing? → Check these 3 things in events.md. Is this an interaction bug? → Check these 3 things in callbacks.md.' The current 6.6KB SKILL.md should be under 2KB. Second: add a 'Top 10 FullCalendar Bugs' section directly in SKILL.md with the fix for each. The critical rules are a start but miss recurring events, timezone issues, DST transitions, allDay slot vs timed events, and the `eventDataTransform` gotcha. Third: the reference files are all ~7KB with no consistent structure. Standardize them: Overview, Common Patterns, Common Mistakes, Code Examples. Fourth: the HTMX integration section should be a standalone pattern, not woven into the core concepts. Most users won't use HTMX. Fifth: add one complete, copy-pasteable example in SKILL.md — a minimal working calendar with a JSON feed, event click handling, and a toolbar. That single example would teach more than 40KB of reference docs. Everything else is optimization.

peer_reviews.strongest: The Executor — the 'Top 10 FullCalendar Bugs' idea is the highest-leverage single improvement. It directly addresses the skill's biggest weakness (agents can't troubleshoot without reading 40KB) with minimal effort. The decision-tree restructure is also practical and immediately actionable.
peer_reviews.biggest_blind_spot: The Expansionist — the accessibility and mobile points are valid but expanding scope without fixing the foundation is how skills become bloated and useless. Adding Playwright testing patterns is a separate skill, not an improvement to this one.
peer_reviews.what_all_missed: None of the reviewers addressed the skill's eval coverage. The evals.json is a single file with no test scenarios — this means the skill can't be validated or improved quantitatively. Every reviewer should have flagged this.

peer_reviews.strongest: The First Principles Thinker — correctly identifies that the skill's unique value isn't mirroring FullCalendar's docs (which already exist) but bridging the integration gap. The 'reorganize around integration scenarios, not API surfaces' insight is the strategic fix that makes all other improvements coherent.
peer_reviews.biggest_blind_spot: The Contrarian — correctly identifies the structural problem but the proposed solution (inline everything) would make SKILL.md 40KB and worse. The answer isn't to eliminate reference files; it's to make SKILL.md a better index and make the reference files more scannable.
peer_reviews.what_all_missed: The skill's description/triggering is too narrow. It says 'Use when tasks involve FullCalendar' but doesn't mention common failure modes that should trigger it: calendar not rendering, events not showing, wrong date display, drag-drop not working. These are the real-world triggers.

peer_reviews.strongest: The Outsider — the 'zero code examples' finding is damning. Every effective skill has at least one copy-pasteable example. The observation that the skill 'reads like it was written by someone who knows FullCalendar very well and forgot what it's like to not know it' is the most important sentence in this entire debate.
peer_reviews.biggest_blind_spot: The Executor — the '200-line decision tree' idea is good but undersells the problem. It's not just about routing; it's about giving the agent enough context to make the right routing decision. A decision tree without context is just another index.
peer_reviews.what_all_missed: The skill has no version pinning guidance. It says 'v6' but doesn't specify which minor version, and FullCalendar v6 has had breaking changes between minors. An agent following this skill might install v6.1 and get different behavior than v6.3.

peer_reviews.strongest: The Contrarian — the timezone and recurring events gap is the most critical missing content. These aren't edge cases; they're the two features that cause the most production bugs in any calendar application. The skill's silence on these is a real failure.
peer_reviews.biggest_blind_spot: The First Principles Thinker — the 'reorganize around integration scenarios' idea is strategically sound but operationally vague. What scenarios? How many? Without concrete examples, this is a direction, not a plan. The executor's decision tree is the tactical implementation of this strategy.
peer_reviews.what_all_missed: The skill doesn't address the CDN vs ES6 bundle tradeoffs in any meaningful way. The CDN bundle is easier but the ES6 bundle is tree-shakeable. For performance-sensitive apps, this matters. The skill should guide the agent on which to choose and when.

peer_reviews.strongest: The Expansionist — the accessibility point alone justifies this review. FullCalendar accessibility is a minefield and the skill's complete silence on it means agents will build inaccessible calendars. The mobile point is equally strong — every calendar needs to work on phones.
peer_reviews.biggest_blind_spot: The Outsider — the 'put task routing at the top' suggestion is too simplistic. Task routing is useful for agents but useless for humans reading the skill. The skill serves both audiences and should be structured accordingly, not just optimized for agent scanning.
peer_reviews.what_all_missed: The skill has no migration guidance. Users upgrading from FullCalendar v5 to v6 face breaking changes. An agent working on a v5→v6 migration needs specific guidance, and the skill provides none. This is a common real-world scenario that's completely unaddressed.

chairman_verdict.agrees: The council unanimously agrees on three things: (1) SKILL.md is a poor entry point that forces agents to read 40KB+ of reference files for basic tasks — it needs to be a decision tree with inline troubleshooting, not a table of contents. (2) The skill is missing critical real-world content: timezone handling, recurring events, accessibility, and version-specific guidance. (3) The reference files, while individually decent, lack consistent structure and should be standardized with Common Patterns and Common Mistakes sections. There is also unanimous agreement that the eval coverage is inadequate — the skill cannot be validated or quantitatively improved without proper test scenarios.
chairman_verdict.clashes: The council clashes on scope. The Expansionist wants to add accessibility, mobile, testing, and framework connector guidance — effectively doubling the skill's scope. The Executor and Contrarian want to ruthlessly focus on making the existing content more accessible and actionable. The Chairman's view: scope expansion is warranted only for accessibility (which is a correctness issue, not a nice-to-have) and mobile responsiveness (which affects a majority of real-world calendars). Testing patterns and framework connector detection belong in separate skills. The council also clashes on reorganization strategy: the First Principles Thinker wants scenario-based restructuring while the Executor wants a decision tree. These are complementary — the decision tree in SKILL.md routes to scenario-based reference files.
chairman_verdict.blind_spots: The council caught several collective blind spots: (1) No reviewer addressed the skill's triggering description — it should include failure-mode triggers like 'calendar not rendering' or 'events displaying on wrong dates'. (2) No reviewer questioned whether the reference file split is optimal — seven files might be too many, or too few. (3) No reviewer addressed the skill's relationship to FullCalendar's own documentation — it should link to official docs for API details and focus on integration patterns. (4) The CDN vs ES6 bundle tradeoff was only mentioned by one reviewer.
chairman_verdict.recommendation: Restructure in three phases. Phase 1 (immediate): Rewrite SKILL.md as a decision-tree index with inline 'Top 10 Bugs' section, one complete copy-pasteable example, and a version-pinning note. Move the Critical Rules to the top. Phase 2 (short-term): Standardize all reference files with consistent structure (Overview, Patterns, Mistakes, Examples). Add timezone and recurring events guidance to events.md. Add accessibility and mobile guidance to views.md and display.md. Phase 3 (medium-term): Add proper eval scenarios that test whether an agent can build, debug, and integrate a calendar. Expand the skill description to include failure-mode triggers. Add migration guidance for v5→v6.
chairman_verdict.first_step: Rewrite SKILL.md to lead with a decision-tree routing table, inline the top 10 FullCalendar bugs with fixes, and add one complete minimal working example (CDN + JSON feed + event click). This single change would make the skill 10x more effective without touching any reference file. Estimated effort: 2-3 hours.
